chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of our companions,

Regarding a man who visits the House (Kabah), so he sleeps in the road, he said: ‘If he spent the night in Makkah, then upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal); but if it was such that he had exited from it, then there is nothing upon him, and even if in the morning he is in besides Mina’. And in another report from Abul Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who visits (the Kabah) but he sleeps in besides Mina, he said: ‘When he exceeds Aqaba Al-Medinayn, then there is no problem if he sleeps’.

key_terms.زَارَ الْبَيْتَ: Visited the House (performed Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.عَقَبَةَ الْمَدَنِيِّينَ: Aqaba of the Medinans (a specific location/landmark in Mina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who sleeps in the road during Hajj instead of staying in Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the geographical boundaries for the obligatory night stay in Mina, establishing that the penalty of dam applies only if the pilgrim remains within Makkah's limits rather than having truly departed for Mina. The second narration further refines this by identifying 'Aqaba al-Madinayn' as the critical threshold for validity, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise spatial definitions in ritual law. This ruling underscores the principle that the obligation is tied to the intentional transition from the holy city to the plain of Mina, rather than mere proximity.
